subject: PO/Marketplace rate-card alignment — next steps & unit-price scenarios
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Rao <amit@cloudbridge.io>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@acmetech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO/Marketplace rate-card alignment — next steps & unit-price scenarios

Hi Amit / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick post-call recap + concrete next steps so we stay aligned on the PO/private-offer mapping exercise we discussed.

Call highlights (short):
- Acme Tech expected monthly active inference: ~120M tokens (mixed short/medium sequences) with seasonal spikes to ~220M.
- FY28 budget band discussed: $10k–$35k/month (target avg $/1M tokens is what your finance team will use for comparisons).
- Priority: land an AWS Marketplace private offer that maps to a predictable per-token unit rate (target $/1M tokens), with fallbacks to our hosted API if private SKU limits cause throttling.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Amit: can you confirm marketplace constraints around minimum unit granularity and whether you can create multiple SKUs (commit tiers) inside a single private offer?
2) Priya: please confirm your expected committed monthly spend tier (low/mid/high) and whether Acme will sign a 12-month vs 24-month PO — this changes the unit economics materially.
3) Redwood (Karthik/Ben): we will share a short workbook that maps three unit-price scenarios to 1M-token buckets and shows the net monthly spend at the volumes you shared. See attached: acme_usage_profile.csv + redwood_unit_price_scenarios.xlsx.

Target financial framing: our goal for this exercise is to land a unit price reference for procurement that looks like $/1M tokens (examples below). We will provide both list and discounted private-offer mappings.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the workbook in the next email.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Attachments: acme_usage_profile.csv (usage export), call_recording_link_stub

From: Amit Rao <amit@cloudbridge.io>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 18:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: PO/Marketplace rate-card alignment — next steps & unit-price scenarios

Kimberly — thanks for the clear write-up. Quick answers from the partner side: 

- Marketplace SKU granularity: AWS Marketplace private offers allow multiple SKUs, but each SKU is a separate billable line item; partners commonly create 2–3 commit SKUs (e.g., base, mid, enterprise). Minimum granularity is at SKU/usage-level; you cannot create dynamic per-token pricing without mapping it to a SKU that tracks usage units.

- Private offer constraints: we can do different unit multipliers (e.g., per 1M tokens mapped to a consumption SKU) but the buyer’s procurement often expects a single reference unit for comparisons. So the mapping workbook you mentioned is exactly the right play.

- On commitments: Acme’s procurement prefers 12-months with quarterly reviews. Priya — can you confirm if that’s a hard ask? Also need to confirm whether they want invoicing via marketplace or direct invoices to Acme finance.

I’ll coordinate with CloudBridge marketplace ops to draft a PO SKU layout once you share the workbook.

Thanks,
Amit
Partnerships, CloudBridge
amit@cloudbridge.io

Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: RE: PO/Marketplace rate-card alignment — next steps & unit-price scenarios

Priya / Amit — attached is the workbook I promised (redwood_unit_price_scenarios.xlsx). I populated three scenarios (Conservative / Target / Aggressive) using Acme’s usage profile. Highlights below.

Quick summary (all numbers expressed as $ per 1M tokens):
- Conservative (no commitment): $1,600 / 1M tokens (hosted list rate translated to 1M unit) — expected monthly spend @120M = $192k
- Target (12-month committed tier): $650 / 1M tokens (requires ~100M+ monthly commit) — expected monthly spend @120M = $78k
- Aggressive (higher commit / 24-month): $400 / 1M tokens (100M+ commit with quantization/latency-copilot optimizations) — expected monthly spend @120M = $48k

Notes / mapping guidance for Marketplace private offer: 
- Recommend creating 3 SKUs: "Base-Consumption (per 1M)" (Conservative), "Commit-12M (per 1M)" (Target), "Commit-24M (per 1M)" (Aggressive). Each SKU should map usage to the 1M-token unit we show in the workbook.
- If AWS Marketplace requires a different billing unit (e.g., per-100k tokens), we can convert programmatically but the procurement sheet must show the normalized $/1M for easy comparison.
- Fallback policy: set the private-offer limit to the committed SKU and allow overflow to route to Redwood hosted API at the Conservative rate so there's never a service interruption.

Next steps (action owners):
- Amit (CloudBridge): confirm whether you can create the 3 SKUs inside a single private offer and whether marketplace ops need any additional metadata from Acme.
- Priya (Acme): confirm commitment term (12 vs 24) and preferred invoicing path (marketplace vs direct).
- Ben/Karthik (Redwood): once we have term, Redwood will generate the private_offer_template.docx and a DocuSign-ready PO for Acme. We will also attach the HubSpot deal (DEAL-4782).

Attachments: redwood_unit_price_scenarios.xlsx (pricing scenarios), acme_usage_profile.csv (source), private_offer_template.docx (placeholder PO).

Happy to hop on a 20-min sync if this needs a quick alignment call — I’m free Mon 9–11 PT.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
